--- order: 4 unit: build introduces: [input-value] assumes: [js-event, text-content, js-query] title: "Inputs" summary: "Read what someone types with .value, react as they type, and turn text into a number with Number()." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 12 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "", zoom: 1.4} caption: ".value is what the person typed, and it is always text" say: "Dot value is what the person typed, and it is always text." clip: - caption: "An input box, a button, and a place for the answer." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "\n\n

\n", append: true} - caption: text: "nameBox.value is whatever is typed in the box right now." say: "name Box dot value is whatever is typed in the box right now." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "\n", append: true} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 750 - caption: "Type a name, then click Greet." - wait: 750 hook: "A calculator on a web page reads what you typed, then answers. You'll build one." --- An input box has a **value**: whatever is typed in it right now. Read it inside a handler: ```js out.textContent = "Hello, " + nameBox.value + "!"; ``` Two events are useful: `"click"` on a button, and `"input"` on the box itself, which fires on **every keystroke**. **The hard part** is that `.value` is always **text**, even when someone types a number. `"4" + "5"` is `"45"`, not 9. Turn it into a number first: `Number(a.value)`. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict check: type: predict q: "You type Sam in the box and click Greet. What does the paragraph say?" options: ["Hello, Sam!", "Hello, nameBox.value!", "Hello, !", "Nothing: a script cannot read a box"] actual: "Hello, Sam! nameBox.value is read at the moment of the click, and + joins the three pieces of text." ``` When is `nameBox.value` read: when the page loads, or when the button is clicked? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I typed in the box and watched the character count change on every keystroke." } ``` Press **Run**, then type in the box. The count changes on every keystroke, because the listener is on the `"input"` event. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: ".value is the text typed so far, and an input event fires on every keystroke; because it is text, turn it into a number with Number() before doing sums." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each piece with what it does." pairs: - ["msg.addEventListener(\"input\", …)", "runs on every keystroke in the box"] - ["msg.value", "the text in the box right now"] - ["msg.value.length", "how many characters are in the box"] - ["Number(a.value)", "turns the typed text into a number"] - check: type: question q: "Someone types 4 and 5 in two boxes, and you write a.value + b.value. What do you get?" options: ["\"45\", because the values are text", "9", "An error", "0"] answer: 0 explain: "The value of an input is always text, so + joins the two pieces of text: \"4\" + \"5\" is \"45\". Number(a.value) + Number(b.value) is 9." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "The page shows 45 instead of 9. There is no red error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 9 fault: logic misconception: value-is-text explain: "a.value and b.value are text, so + joins them. Turn each into a number first: Number(a.value) + Number(b.value)." ``` ### Which part does what? Match code with meaning. ### 4 and 5 What + does to text. ### Spot the bug The sum is wrong, and nothing complains. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Number() turns typed text into a number so sums work; an if inside the handler reacts to what was typed." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } tasks: - hint: - "The page is adding text. What does + do with text?" - "Wrap each value in Number(...): Number(a.value) + Number(b.value)." expected: page.html#sol-add try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#bug", height: 430 } check: { type: code, text: "Make the Add button show 9 for 4 + 5.", rules: { contains: ["Number("] } } - hint: - "An if inside the handler can look at how many characters there are." - "Add a paragraph for the warning, and if (msg.value.length > 20) { … } to fill it." expected: page.html#sol-limit check: { type: code, text: "Show Too long! in red when the message has more than 20 characters.", rules: { contains: ["if (", "20"] } } ``` ### Make Add add Numbers, not text. ### A length limit Decide as they type. ## Make: a calculator of your own ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: read an input, turn it into a number, work something out and show it on the page." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I made a calculator or converter that reads a box, uses Number(), and shows the answer." } ``` Make a small tool that reads a **number** from a box and shows an answer: a tip calculator, a temperature converter (°C to °F), an age-in-days counter, a unit converter. Check for a bad number with `isNaN(...)`, as the page on this lesson does. ## Change a bill splitter ```step stage: modify try: { playground: dom, starter: "bill.html#bill", height: 460 } hint: "Add a third box with its own `id`, read it with `Number(...)` like the other two, and work the tip out before you divide." check: type: code text: "Add a tip box, and include the tip in what each person pays." rules: { contains: ['id="tip"', '#tip'] } ``` This page splits a restaurant bill between friends. It reads two boxes, checks that they hold sensible numbers and shows each person's share. Add a third box for a tip in percent, and make each share include it. For a $60 bill with a 10% tip and 4 people, each person should pay $16.50. ```code bill.html#bill

Split the bill

Bill: $ People:

``` ```code bill.html#sol-bill

Split the bill

Bill: $ Tip %: People:

``` ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "You want to add a new line to a list every time someone clicks Add. What must your code make?" options: ["A new element, then put it into the page", "A new variable called list", "A new input", "A new class"] answer: 0 explain: "The page only changes when your code changes it. To add a line, make a new element and add it to the list. Next lesson." ``` You can now read what people type. Next: **build a list on the page**. ```teacher summary: Students read an input with .value, react as they type with the input event, find that values are text and use Number() to add, and make a calculator or converter of their own. time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can read what someone types with .value. - I can react on every keystroke with the input event. - I can turn typed text into a number with Number(). before: > Read the unit primer first. This is the Python input() lesson with a twist: there is no program waiting, so the page reacts to an event. `input` fires on every keystroke; `click` on a button reads the box once. The big idea is that `.value` is always text, as `input()` was in Python: the same `"45"` surprise. The bug has no red error, so students must read the answer. `Number("abc")` is `NaN`; `isNaN(x)` checks for it, used in the Make example. The playground cannot send a form, on purpose: use a button and an event, not a `
`. running: - "Predict: ask when the value is read." - "Run: ask students to type quickly and say when the number changes." - "Investigate: ask what + does to two pieces of text." - 'Modify: ask what Number("5") gives, and what Number("hello") gives.' - "Make: ask each student what could go wrong if someone types words." stuck: - see: The sum shows 45, or the text joined. ask: Is the value turned into a number first? fix: "Wrap each value: Number(a.value)." - see: Cannot read properties of null (reading value). ask: Does the input id match the selector? fix: "Match the id exactly, with #." - see: The box seems to do nothing. ask: Is the listener on the box or the button, and is it the right event? fix: Use "input" on the box, or "click" on the button. - see: NaN is shown. ask: Was the box empty or full of words? fix: Check with isNaN and show a friendly message. stretch: Make the result appear live, with no button at all, using the input event on each box. support: Give the greeting page and ask students to change only the words, then add a second box. leads: "Next lesson: lists of elements: making new elements and adding them to the page." exit: q: Why is "4" + "5" equal to "45"? a: The value of an input is text, and + joins text. Number() turns it into a number first. explain: | 1. `box.value` is the text typed in the box right now. 2. The `"input"` event runs your function on every keystroke. 3. A value is always text: use `Number(box.value)` for sums. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-add step-4#t2: page.html#sol-limit step-5: page.html#sol-make step-6: bill.html#sol-bill struggle: 'Text versus number: "4" + "5" is "45". Show the page, ask what + does to text, and only then show Number().' ```
